collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A big storm is coming and the children are frightened: chant together while tying down the huts, or tell storm stories inside.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The sky has turned a strange green and the wind is rising fast. The adults are tying down roofs and the children are frightened. (friend) is clinging to (subject)'s leg and will not let go. (subject) needs both hands for the ropes. How should (subject) help (friend) through the storm?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) teaches (friend) the stormwatchers' chant: pull, tie, hold, stay. They chant it together, louder each time the wind gusts, and (friend) holds the end of every rope (subject) ties. One roof blows off anyway. But (friend) is too busy chanting to cry, and afterward tells everyone (friend.he/she) helped hold the village down.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) takes (friend) and the other children into the strongest hut and tells them every storm story (subject.he/she) knows, the funny ones, the brave ones, the one about the goat that rode out a storm on a roof. The wind howls all night. In the morning, the children are asleep in a pile, and the goat is still on the roof.
